messages.content: "John has decided to invest in two different funds. He invested $5000 in Fund A which has an annual return rate of 7% and he plans to keep his money there for 5 years. On the other hand, he invested $8000 in Fund B with an annual return rate of 5% for a period of 7 years. Can you predict the profit John will make from both Fund A and Fund B?"

function.name: investment_predictProfit
function.description: Predict the profit for given investment after specified number of years. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

annual_return.description: The annual return rate of the investment. This is a float type value.

years.description: The time period in years for which the investment is made.

message.reasoning: We need to use the tool to predict profit for each fund. The tool signature: investment_predictProfit takes investment_amount, annual_return, years. It returns any. We need to call the tool twice: one for Fund A, one for Fund B. Then we need to respond with the predicted profits. The user wants the profit John will make from both Fund A and Fund B. So we need to compute profit = investment_amount * ((1 + annual_return) ** years - 1). But we rely on the tool. So we call the tool for each fund. Then we need to respond with the results. The tool returns any; we need to parse the result. The tool might return a number or an object. We need to handle that. We'll call the tool for Fund A: investment_amount=5000, annual_return=0.07, years=5. Then for Fund B: investment_amount=8000, annual_return=0.05, years=7. Then we need to respond with the predicted profits. The user wants the profit from both funds. So we need to provide the profit amounts. Possibly we need to format them nicely.
